title: KOH-activated  Spirulina  sp. biochar: a sustainable biosorbent for removal of hexavalent chromium( vi ) from water
content: Global dependence on unsustainable heavy metal treatment technologies threatens ecological resilience and necessitates the development of circular, biomass-based alternatives. In this context, Spirulina sp. (SP) microalgal biomass with reactive functional groups on its cell walls offers an efficient, renewable and environmentally friendly adsorbent for heavy metal remediation. This study explores the comparative Cr(vi) adsorption potential of untreated and KOH activated Spirulina sp. biomass. The activation process resulted in an increased surface area, heterogeneous pore distribution, and higher density of hydroxyl groups as corroborated by SEM, BET, FT-IR and XRD analyses. Among the synthesized biochars, S–KOH1:3 was selected owing to its superior removal potential compared to other formulations for further adsorption experimentation. Batch adsorption analysis showed a higher Cr(vi) adsorption potential of 9.019 mg g−1 for S–KOH1:3 compared to 6.971 mg g−1 for SP. Chemisorption predominated on adsorbent surfaces and the dominant mechanisms involved in Cr(vi) removal were reduction, chemisorption and electrostatic interaction. Continuous column studies revealed that S–KOH1:3 exhibited significantly prolonged breakthrough time and at a 1.0 cm bed depth, the breakthrough time increased from 56.0 min (SP) to 170.3 min (S–KOH1:3). Reusability studies demonstrated practical regeneration, reinforcing its suitability as an economical and sustainable biosorbent for wastewater treatment.
